title: Read the public contract first
summary: Map every service operation to its input, result, and owner before opening an implementation.
body:
Three names, three jobs

The target architecture is backend-agnostic. A feature imports sdk-api and sdk-model: it asks a DetailsService for content and receives StreamCoreContent. It does not know which backend supplied that content. RuntimeDetailsService is the internal implementation that enforces account/profile authorization and content policy. DetailsProvider is the provider integration contract that obtains backend data. The provider module implements that contract and hides its DTOs, network client, credentials, and mapping.

An interface is useful here because there are two actual boundaries: application to SDK, and runtime to backend. It is not a rule to create an interface for every class. Runtime services, identity helpers, and state management stay concrete and internal. Local library, history, and progress have stores because they are SDK-owned persistence; they do not acquire artificial backend providers.

RuntimeStreamCoreClient constructs one shared RuntimeSession, one authentication service, and the domain services. The same RuntimePlaybackService instance backs client.playback and supplies progress to RuntimeLibraryService. The client delegates close; authentication restoration is implemented directly by RuntimeAuthService. The client does not receive callbacks from services to run their workflows.

The complete service operation map

Unless stated otherwise, suspend operations return StreamCoreResult<T>. The table shows T, not a promise that the operation succeeds. Profile IDs remain explicit so the SDK can reject a mismatched request.

SurfaceOperations and inputsSuccessful value
Clientclose()Unit, synchronously.
AuthenticationrestoreSession(), login(identifier, password), loginWithQr(qrCode), logout(), recoverPassword(email, otp?)StreamCoreContext for restoration; Unit for the other operations. Account state comes from context.
Profile entrybeginEntry(), selectProfile(profileId), confirmPin(challengeId, pin), synchronous cancelPin(challengeId), clearSelection()StreamCoreProfileEntryResult, StreamCoreProfileSelectionResult, StreamCoreProfile, Unit, Unit.
Profile managementgetProfiles(), getProfileEditorOptions(), createProfile(StreamCoreCreateProfile), updateProfile(StreamCoreUpdateProfile), deleteProfile(profileId)Profile list, StreamCoreProfileEditorOptions, created/updated profile, Unit.
Home and detailsgetCollections(profileId); getDetails(profileId, contentId); getRecommendations(profileId, contentId)List of StreamCoreCollection; StreamCoreContent; content list.
Searchsearch(profileId, query, interaction), loadTrending(profileId), displayedResults(profileId, query, results, interaction), resultSelected(profileId, query)Content lists for retrieval; Unit for interaction recording. StreamCoreSearchInteraction distinguishes typing, submission, and recent selection.
Search historyobserveHistory(profileId), recordHistory(profileId, query), removeHistoryQuery(profileId, query), clearHistory(profileId)Flow of results containing string lists; mutations return Unit.
Libraryobserve(profileId), observeContentState(profileId, contentId), setLiked(profileId, content, isLiked), setInMyList(profileId, content, isInMyList)Flows of results containing StreamCoreLibrary or StreamCoreContentLibraryState; mutations return Unit.
Playback and progressresolveSource(StreamCorePlaybackRequest), synchronous createProgressRecorder(request, initialPositionMillis), observeProgress(profileId), getProgress(profileId, contentId), updateProgress(entry), removeProgress(profileId, contentId)StreamCorePlaybackMedia, a PlaybackProgressRecorder, flow of progress-entry lists, nullable StreamCorePlaybackProgressEntry, Unit, Unit.
RecorderreportEvent(StreamCorePlaybackProgressEvent, positionMillis, durationMillis)Unit: policy may save, remove, or intentionally ignore the event.

Models carry values; context carries authority

StreamCoreConfiguration identifies backend/environment, locale, account restriction, and persistence mode. StreamCoreCapabilities describes supported operations, including distinct search/history flags and playback support. StreamCoreContext exposes account, authorized profile, isAuthInitialized/isClosed flags, and profileActivationId. A profile or content value obtained elsewhere does not confer authorization.

StreamCoreContent is shared catalogue metadata. StreamCorePlaybackRequest carries profile/content IDs and a content snapshot, while StreamCorePlaybackMedia describes a resolved asset. Resolution checks authoritative catalogue content; a snapshot cannot grant access. StreamCorePlaybackProgressEntry adds position, duration, and timestamp. StreamCoreLibrary groups continue-watching, liked, and my-list content; applications choose their presentation.

Pure helpers are also public API

LoginValidator.validate and ProfileValidator.validate provide form feedback. SearchQueryNormalizer.normalize collapses whitespace; isSearchable uses a three-character minimum. PlaybackProgressPolicy.isResumable requires positive duration, at least 30 seconds, and less than 95% completion. Runtime repeats enforcement; using these helpers in a ViewModel does not bypass it.

StreamCoreResult separates expected success and typed failure. Branch on StreamCoreError types and structured details, not diagnostic text. Unsupported, PinRejected, Authentication, and SessionExpired mean different things. Cancellation still throws; constructors and host callbacks are not made exception-free by this result type.

Read/change exercise. Trace getDetails from interface to runtime to provider. For a new backend field, decide whether it belongs in an internal DTO or the shared model. Only promote it if consumers need a provider-neutral meaning. For a new access rule, locate the runtime enforcement point before adding another layer.

quiz.question: Which type should a feature consume for catalogue detail access?
options: The backend repository and its DTO
quiz.explanation: The consumer service is the public application boundary. Runtime enforces shared rules; the provider integration remains behind it.

title: Follow one client from construction to close
summary: Session restoration, login, logout, and close change different state. Cancellation does not imply rollback.
body:
Construction does not log in

The client factory assembles dependencies without network requests. Initial context has no account and isAuthInitialized = false; this is not a completed logged-out decision. The host explicitly calls sdk.auth.restoreSession(), handles its StreamCoreResult<StreamCoreContext>, observes context, and starts profile entry when an account is available. Direct login is also valid without a prior restore call; it initializes authentication through the same installation path.

RuntimeAuthService implements AuthService.restoreSession() directly and serializes restoration, login, and logout with the session's authenticationMutex. ensureContextStorageAvailable() runs the storage bundle's checkContextStorage callback before those workflows and sets contextStorageChecked only after success. A failed check returns immediately and can be retried. It probes auth/context storage so browser startup can choose session fallback before authentication; it does not parse or convert library/history/progress. restoreSession() then calls AuthProvider.restoreSession(), which returns the backend StreamCoreResult<StreamCoreAuthState>. Once authentication is initialized, even by direct login, restoration returns the current context without repeating backend restoration. The availability check remains internal; there is no client forwarding wrapper.

Installing an account has a commit order

  1. Validate the provider's account ID. Blank IDs produce Parsing; an expectedAccountId mismatch invalidates the provider session and returns Unauthorized.
  2. Create account-bound adapters through ProviderSessionFactory; this construction must not fetch network data.
  3. Install a new AccountSession, remove old profile authorization, and mark authentication initialization incomplete.
  4. Clear the persisted selected-profile reference. Only after that write succeeds does runtime mark authentication initialized.

The context projection hides the account while installation is incomplete. A storage failure can therefore leave committed provider credentials but no published account and no profile grant. A later auth.restoreSession() can retry. Persisted profile selection is deliberately not restored as authorization.

Login returns an operation result; context tells you the state

Credential login checks capability and required fields, trims the identifier, and preserves password contents. QR login checks its own capability and trims its code. Recovery checks capability and a nonblank email; it does not install an account. Successful login reads the provider's committed authState.value and installs it through the same path as restoration.

If login fails, runtime reconciles that provider state before returning the original failure. If cancellation occurs, reconciliation runs in NonCancellable and cancellation is rethrown. Consequently, a cancelled account-B login can still leave account B installed if the provider already committed it. The old profile grant remains revoked. Treating cancellation as transaction rollback would misrepresent the actual account.

Logout is conditional; close is final

EventCurrent behavior
Logout returns Network or another non-session failureKeep the runtime account/profile for retry. An unsuccessful request is not proof that remote logout happened.
Logout is cancelledReconcile provider auth state, then propagate cancellation. A still-logged-in provider preserves access; an authoritatively logged-out provider clears it.
Logout succeeds or returns SessionExpiredAttempt selection cleanup; SessionExpired also invokes provider invalidation. Clear runtime account/profile in finally. Return the original logout result if cancellation does not escape.
CloseAtomically mark this instance closed and remove account/profile/challenge state, cancel owned work, and release resources once.

There is a subtle logout detail: the normal cleanup block returns a result, but logout does not substitute that result for the provider's logout result. A mapped cleanup failure still reaches clearAccount(). Cancellation during cleanup propagates, also after clearing access. Library, history, and progress remain account-owned; neither successful logout nor close erases them.

close() is idempotent and does not perform remote logout. In-flight work may receive cancellation; later guarded requests fail Closed. The context StateFlow stays collectable, so the host must cancel its own collectors. A closed instance cannot reopen.

Read/change exercise. Compare the two logout cancellation tests: one provider keeps its state, the other clears it before throwing. If changing cleanup, preserve both outcomes and verify the observable context as well as the thrown exception.

quiz.question: A logout coroutine is cancelled after the provider publishes LoggedOut. What should the host expect?
options: Cancellation restores the previous account automatically
Cancellation propagates, and context reflects the cleared account
A successful Unit result replaces cancellation
quiz.explanation: Runtime reconciles committed provider state in NonCancellable, then rethrows cancellation. Cancellation is not rollback.

title: Separate profile metadata from authorization
summary: Understand why Ready, ChooseProfile, and PinRequired are different outcomes, and exactly when a grant appears.
body:
Management needs an account; content needs a grant

getProfiles(), editor options, and CRUD operate on the authenticated account. Editing another owned profile does not require activating it. withAccountProfile fetches the current list to verify ownership for update/delete; deletion also enforces canDelete. Creating a profile does not activate it.

Create/update fetch current StreamCoreProfileEditorOptions, validate a trimmed nonblank name of at most 32 characters, and check avatar/parental-level membership. The inputs contain IDs, not backend DTOs. Provider rank values are not a universal age algorithm; isKidsProfile expresses provider policy. Successful updates reconcile the active grant. A changed PIN policy revokes it; other changed profile metadata replaces it with a new activation.

Entry is a decision, not a list fetch

beginEntry() starts a fresh selection attempt and immediately revokes old authorization and challenges. It then fetches profiles. Use it after login or fresh session restoration. Use getProfiles() for chooser/editor refreshes: that reconciles changed or deleted profiles without automatically selecting one.

Entry outcomeMeaning and application action
StreamCoreProfileEntryNoProfilesNo profiles exist. Present the empty/create flow.
StreamCoreProfileEntryChooseProfileMultiple profiles exist. Show the supplied list; no authorization exists yet.
StreamCoreProfileEntryReadyThe singleton is already activated. Navigate; do not select it again.
StreamCoreProfileEntryPinRequiredA challenge exists. Present PIN input; challenge metadata grants no content access.

StreamCoreProfileEntryResult covers all four. Explicit selectProfile(id) returns StreamCoreProfileSelectionResult, whose two implementations are the same Ready and PinRequired classes. Selection also starts a new attempt, even for the same ID. For an unprotected profile, runtime calls provider selection, verifies the returned ID, checks whether a PIN policy appeared, and only then tries authorization.

PIN confirmation is a guarded sequence

StreamCoreProfilePinPolicy declares a positive ASCII digit count. It contains no PIN, cooldown, or persistent grant. StreamCoreProfilePinChallenge contains an opaque challenge ID, profile metadata, and that digit count. Keep the PIN draft in transient application state.

  1. Confirm capability, current challenge identity, exact length, and ASCII digits. Invalid input never reaches provider verification.
  2. Create a distinct ProfilePinVerification identity and install it only while the captured challenge/selection is current.
  3. Fetch profiles again. Missing profile or changed PIN policy expires the attempt. Check verification identity before calling the provider.
  4. Call verifyProfilePin. Wrong PIN is PinRejected, not account SessionExpired. On success, check coroutine activity and identity again.
  5. Call provider selection; require the expected profile ID and unchanged PIN policy. Persist selected-profile reference, check cancellation, then atomically publish AuthorizedProfile.

Persistence precedes authorization. A storage failure must not publish a grant even after the backend accepted the PIN. Network and storage failures can leave the same challenge retryable. The finally block clears only this verification identity, so it cannot erase a newer attempt. Successful confirmation has already updated context; selecting again would revoke it.

Leaving the flow is an explicit state change

cancelPin(challengeId) invalidates the matching challenge immediately. If confirmation commits after cancellation captured that challenge, it can also revoke the grant associated with the same verification. Cancelling only the caller coroutine does not necessarily abandon a still-current challenge; call cancelPin when leaving the PIN flow.

clearSelection() revokes memory before any storage cleanup. A failing or cancelled clear cannot restore access. Reload the chooser with getProfiles; protected re-entry needs a new challenge. Starting selection through beginEntry/selectProfile has its own cancellation handler that cancels that selection attempt, while confirmPin's finally clears its verification identity.

Read/change exercise. Follow the storage-failure PIN test and mark the exact line where context could first gain a profile. Then move that publication before persistence in your mental model: explain why a failed operation would leave usable authorization. Preserve the existing ordering in any refactor.

quiz.question: beginEntry returns StreamCoreProfileEntryReady. What is the next SDK step before showing content?
options: Call selectProfile with the returned ID again
Persist profileActivationId and restore it next launch
No second selection: Ready already published authorization
quiz.explanation: Ready represents completed activation. Selecting again starts a new attempt and revokes the current grant; activation IDs are never persistent authorization.

title: Read the state machine without inventing layers
summary: One atomic state and a handful of identity objects prevent old work from acting on a new account or profile.
body:
One mutable state, one public projection

RuntimeSession owns a single MutableStateFlow<ClientSessionState>. Authentication/profile services update it atomically; data services use its guards. The ContextStateFlow wrapper computes value directly from the same snapshot and maps/distincts collected snapshots. There is no separately mutable public context or background collector that could lag behind authorization state.

ClientSessionState holds account, authorized profile, selection attempt, challenge, verification, a selection counter, and isAuthInitialized/isClosed flags. withoutProfileAuthorization() clears all profile-related references and increments the counter. It retains the account. The public projection exposes account only when authentication is initialized and derives profileActivationId from the current grant.

Every session type has a concrete job

TypeWhat it carries and why it exists
AccountSessionAccount plus its provider bundle. A new installation creates a new object, even if account IDs match.
ProfileSelectionAttemptAccountSession plus selection version. A later choice supersedes the object, including same-profile re-entry.
PendingProfilePinOne selection attempt plus the public challenge model; derives its account from that attempt.
ProfilePinVerificationOne challenge reference identifying an in-flight confirmation, allowing late or replaced responses to be rejected.
AuthorizedProfileActivation ID, originating attempt, profile metadata, and optional verification identity; derives account/providers through the attempt.
ProviderSessionFactoryPublic integration function that builds adapters for one authenticated account without network work.
ProviderSessionServicesThe account-bound profiles, home, details, search, playback, and content-policy adapters.
ClientSessionState, ContextStateFlow, RuntimeSessionThe atomic record, its public read projection, and the owner of lifecycle/guards respectively.

These internal identity classes are deliberately compared with ===/!==. A data-equal account/profile ID cannot validate an old request. Activation IDs combine a random instance ID and selection version; they help presentation replace observers, but are neither backend tokens nor secrets granting access.

Follow the guard around suspension

withAuthenticatedAccount requires an open client with initialized authentication and the captured account object. It executes work, then reconcileAccountResult checks that account again. An authoritative SessionExpired invalidates only the still-current account under the authentication mutex. An obsolete account-A response cannot log out account B.

withAccountProfile adds nonblank-ID validation and a fresh ownership lookup for management. withAuthorizedProfile is the content/state guard:

  1. profileFailure checks closed/auth-initialization/account/activation state and supplied profile ID.
  2. Fetch provider profiles on every guard invocation. Find the requested profile.
  3. If missing, revoke it. If metadata differs, reconcile it and reject this operation as StaleActivation. A changed PIN policy removes access; another metadata change installs a new grant.
  4. Check the original grant identity, run the domain block, then use checkProfileResult to reject results from a changed account or activation.
Current behavior, not a performance recommendation. The repeated profile fetch is current implementation behavior. Caching it would change when deletion and policy changes take effect. Treat that as a behavior decision with contract tests, not a mechanical optimization. Invalid/unsupported calls can return earlier, and stored-flow emissions do not fetch profiles individually.

Flows and recorders retain their original grant

observeStoredProfileData accepts the authorization captured when the observation method was called. It watches state-derived validity with distinct/flatMapLatest, validates through the fresh-profile guard when starting its valid branch, and checks each stored result against the captured grant. Recollecting that flow cannot bind it to a later activation. The same capture rule applies to playback recorders.

For example, an old profile-P history flow must fail after leaving and re-entering P, although the ID remains P. Create a new flow when profileActivationId changes. This prevents old screens or players from silently writing into a newly authorized session.

The remaining helpers, without mystery

revokeProfile conditionally clears matching access/challenges; reconcileAvailableProfiles handles deleted or changed metadata. The three isCurrent overloads check selection, grant, and verification identity. currentAuthorization exposes the grant to capture now; accountFailure distinguishes incomplete authentication initialization (AuthNotInitialized) from an initialized, unauthenticated account. storageKey builds the configured account/profile partition. filterAllowedContents applies provider policy to successful lists.

executeWhileOpen creates an operation Job linked to the caller and registers cancellation with the SDK-owned SupervisorJob. It disposes that registration and completes the operation in finally. Cancellation propagates; ProviderOperationException preserves its typed error, serialization exceptions become Parsing, and other Exceptions become Unknown. Stored-flow handling instead maps unclassified failures to Storage. These are mappings at specific boundaries, not a claim that every exception is storage or network failure.

clearAccount removes account/profile state and marks authentication initialized. invalidateAccount calls provider invalidation and clears runtime state in finally. File-level invalid, contextFailure, failure, and unsupported construct typed results; they own no state or policy.

Read/change exercise. Trace a suspended details request from account A, then logout/login B before releasing it. Find both identity checks and the test proving B survives A's SessionExpired. When adding a suspend point or store write, ask which captured object must still be current before and after it; do not reacquire current authorization to make an old operation pass.

quiz.question: A history Flow was created during profile activation A. The same profile is entered again as activation B. What happens when the old Flow is recollected?
options: It automatically follows B because the profile ID matches
It remains tied to A and cannot acquire B's authorization
It restores A from persisted profile selection
quiz.explanation: Observation captures the AuthorizedProfile object at method call time. A new activation requires a new observation method call and Flow.
